meta.status: Sources were found by searching WHO, partner and peer-reviewed literature for each technical question (October 2026), starting from the tools that WHO lists in its benchmarks for each technical area. Relevance is judged from each source's title and summary, not from reading every document in full. A source can help answer a question or close the gap behind it; it is not a claim that it raises a JEE score. Questions without a source are shown as 'no source yet'.

solutions.title: Laboratory-acquired infections and pathogen escapes worldwide between 2000 and 2021: a scoping review
solutions.citation: Blacksell SD, Dhawan S, Kusumoto M, et al. Lancet Microbe. 2024;5(2):e194–e202. doi:10.1016/S2666-5247(23)00319-1
solutions.why: Found 309 laboratory-acquired infections and 16 pathogen escapes in public sources over two decades; argues for a formal national and global reporting system because most incidents are never published.

solutions.title: A review of laboratory-acquired infections in the Asia-Pacific: understanding risk and the need for improved biosafety for veterinary and zoonotic diseases
solutions.citation: Siengsanan-Lamont J, Blacksell SD. Trop Med Infect Dis. 2018;3(2):36. doi:10.3390/tropicalmed3020036
solutions.why: Only 27 laboratory infections were reported in the Asia-Pacific in 34 years, mostly from high-income countries; shows under-reporting and the need for incident reporting and training in veterinary and zoonotic labs.

solutions.title: A biosecurity survey in Kenya, November 2014 to February 2015
solutions.citation: Ndhine EO, Slotved HC, Osoro EM, et al. Health Secur. 2016;14(4):205–213. doi:10.1089/hs.2016.0009
solutions.why: Kenyan–Danish survey of 86 laboratories: dangerous agents were held with weak access control and biosafety and biosecurity were often confused; a model for a national baseline before writing legislation and training.

solutions.title: Implementation of bio-risk management system in a national clinical and medical referral centre laboratories
solutions.citation: Lestari F, Kadir A, Miswary T, et al. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2021;18(5):2308.
solutions.why: Gap analysis of Indonesia's national referral laboratories against ISO 35001: over half of elements in place, weakest on leadership, support and performance evaluation; shows how to use the standard as an audit frame.

solutions.title: ISO 35001:2019 Biorisk management for laboratories and other related organisations
solutions.why: International management-system standard for biorisk; gives laboratories and regulators a common frame for audits, competence and continual improvement.

solutions.title: IFBA professional certification in biorisk management
solutions.citation: International Federation of Biosafety Associations (IFBA). Professional certification programme (ISO/IEC 17024).
solutions.why: Internationally recognised certification of individual competence in biorisk management, biosecurity, waste, biosafety cabinets and containment facility operation, with exams in several languages.

solutions.why: Searchable database of the laws and regulations States Parties use to implement the BWC; lets a country compare its biosecurity legislation with others and find gaps.
